notes:
All three MCML workbooks turned out to be FULL LIFE-OF-LOAN schedules recomputed from the original 2017-06-13 financial close / 2017-07-19 first drawdown forward (not stub schedules starting mid-life), so — per the borrower-specific guidance to prioritize accurate row-level overrides over first-principles derivation — each version's params object pins the ENTIRE realized schedule (opening/interest/principal/closing per row, matching the workbook's "Repayment Schedule" sheet exactly) rather than modeling a single rolled-forward disbursement at the effective date as the generic instructions suggested; the three original disbursement tranches (123,820,000 on 2017-07-19; 950,080,000 on 2018-02-20; 196,100,000 on 2018-10-09) are reused unchanged in all three versions since none of the workbooks model a fresh disbursement at the restructure date. "effectiveDate" therefore marks the date each event's new economics visibly take over the schedule, not the schedule's start date. Detail per version:

V1 "1st Restructured" (MCML_Loan_Restructured.xlsx, last modified 2021-06-02 per file metadata): the workbook's own "MCML_Loan" sheet exposes an "Expected Interest Rate" row that steps 7% -> 4% effective the 2018-06-14 quarter (with 2018-03-15 as a blended transition quarter at an implied ~6.65%, folded into the override array as-is), and this reduced 4% rate is carried through to loan maturity (2027-06-15, unchanged tenor). A cell comment on the Summary sheet ("Payment assigned to previous months since restructuring took effect from a previous period") confirms this was applied retroactively. No capitalization or waiver is evident; I classified this RESTRUCTURE (rate change) rather than RATE_CHANGE only because it materially altered installment sizing across the full remaining amortization, but it could reasonably be filed as RATE_CHANGE if the versioning system wants a stricter distinction. No regulatory circular reference is stated anywhere in the workbook (checked cell comments, document properties, all text cells) so left null.

V2 "2nd Restructured Jun'21" (MCML_Loan_2nd Restructured_Jun'21.xlsx, header literally labeled "Proposed 2nd Restructuring"): diverges from V1 starting the 2021-06-15 installment, where scheduled principal (13,823,500.70 in V1) is deferred to 0 for six quarters (2021-06-15 through 2021-12-15), then principal resumes 2022-01-13 at a higher level-principal amount (~15.48M vs ~13.9M) recomputed to still retire the loan by the original 2027-06-15 maturity — i.e. a pure principal moratorium extension with re-leveled installments, no rate change, no capitalization (the deferred quarters' interest was still paid current, per the schedule). Classified MORATORIUM_EXTENSION accordingly. rateBeforePercent/AfterPercent left null since rate is unchanged at 4% throughout.

V3 "3rd Restructured Feb'25" (MCML_Loan_3rd Restructured_Feb'25.xlsx): matches V2 row-for-row through the 2025-01-15 installment, then at 2025-02-13 the opening balance jumps from what would have been 532,014,802.95 (per V2's trajectory) to 697,991,444.16 — a capitalization/overdue roll-in of 165,976,641.21 (computed as the difference; treated as both capitalizedAmount and overdueAmountRolledIn since the workbook doesn't itemize how much of that jump is unpaid interest/LPC vs. deferred principal — flagged as an area of residual uncertainty). Principal is then further deferred (0) for six more quarters (2025-02-13 through 2025-07-15) before resuming 2025-08-14, and the loan is re-amortized out to a new maturity of 2030-07-15 (37 months / ~3 years beyond the original 2027-06-15 maturity), so tenorMonthsAfter=37 (tenorMonthsBefore left null as the "before" tenor at this specific restructure point is ambiguous — it depends on whether you count from original signing or from the 2nd restructure). Rate remains 4% (unchanged) throughout, so rateBeforePercent/AfterPercent are null. No waiver evident (waivedAmount=0) — the full historical amount reappears as principal in the extended schedule, consistent with capitalization rather than forgiveness. No regulatory circular/BB-approval reference found in the workbook text/comments/properties, so left null.

Verification: the last row of V1 and V2 both close to ~0 (fully amortizing, -4e-8 and +1.3e-7 respectively — floating point noise from the workbook's own formulas, not my error), consistent with those versions being superseded before their nominal maturity by the next restructure. V3's last row closes to exactly 0, consistent with it being the final/current version.

All three workbooks' "MCML_Loan" sheet header cells (Loan Amount, Interest Rate 0.07, Maturity date, Number of installments=32) are stale template artifacts NOT updated to reflect the actual restructured terms — I deliberately ignored these headers and relied solely on the "Repayment Schedule" sheet's row-level actuals, per the instruction to prioritize accurate overrides. Cross-checked against frontend/lib/examples.ts EX_DATA['MCML']: that ORIGINAL fixture's own interest_payment_amounts/principal_schedule_amounts overrides match V1/V2's schedules for rows 0-12 (2017-09-14 through 2020-02-13, i.e. still 7%-era + initial 4%-era rows) but diverge from all three restructure files starting row 13 (2020-04-15) onward, implying the ORIGINAL EX_DATA was built from yet another (likely truly-original, un-restructured, 7%-throughout) source for the tail — this pre-existing inconsistency in the ORIGINAL fixture is outside this task's scope but worth flagging to whoever wires these into the versioning engine, since the "original" and "1st restructure" schedules should in principle share row-for-row values through the actual restructure cutover date and currently do not.
